Reason for Socialism: Russian Revolution in 1917.
Das Kapital was written by: Karl Marx.

NM lokhande is known as the "Father of Trade Union Movement". He founded Bombay Mill Association.

In 1924, the party was involved in Kanpur Bolshevik Conspiracy Case — People involved: S A Dange, Muzaffar Ahmed, Shaukat Usmani, etc.

In 1924, Hindustan Republican Association was formed in Kanpur by Ram Prasad Bismil, J. C. Chatterjee, Sachin Sanyal.
In 1925, Kakori Incident/Kakori Train Robbery took place in Kakori, a village near Lucknow.
+ Participants who were hanged
to death: Ashfaqullah Khan, Roshan Singh, Ram Prasad Bismil, and Rajendra Lahiri.
In 1926, Punjab Naujawan Bharat Sabha was formed by Bhagat Singh.
Bhagat Singh fully accepted Marxism.
Hindustan Republican Association (HRA) which was later transformed to Hindustan Socialist Republican Association (HSRA) in 1928 at Feroz Shah Kotla by Chandra Shekhar Azad, Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev.
In 1928, Lala Lajpat Rai protested against Simon Commission and recited slogan "Simon go back". He was hit by Scott during lathi charge due to which he died afterwards.
In 1928, Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev, Raj Guru killed Saunders instead of Scott mistakenly in Lahore to avenge the death of Lala Lajpat Rai. rs: MUJHE KYU TODA?
On April 8, 1929, Bhagat Singh and Batukeshwer Dutt bombed Central Legislative Assembly.
(1928) as it was Anti-National (as said by Swaraj Party) and Trade Disputes Bill (1929).
Purpose: No to kill anyone but To Make Deaf Hear.
Outcome: They did not run away; they surrendered to use the court as a platform to spread their ideology.
In 1929, Chandra Shekar Azad was involved in the conspiracy to blow up Lord Irwin's train, unfortunately the plan failed.
Hunger Strike (1929-30):
Issue: Bhagat Singh and other revolutionaries demanded the status of political prisoners (better food, books, no discrimination), which was denied.
1st Hunger Strike (June 1929): Jatindra Nath Das died on 13 September 1929 after a 63-day fast. The British conceded some demands but later failed to fully implement them.
2nd Hunger Strike (1930): Launched due to the British reneging on earlier assurances.
Lahore Conspiracy Case Trial:
A special ordinance (1930) was issued by the Viceroy to conduct the trial without normal procedures, allowing it to proceed even in the absence of the accused (due to boycott).
Approvers (Government Witnesses): Hans Raj Vohra, Jai Gopal, Phanindranath Ghosh, Sobha Singh.

Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev Thapar and Shivaram Rajguru, were hanged by British authorities on March 23, 1931, in Lahore Jail, a day ahead of schedule. Convicted in the Lahore Conspiracy Case for killing British police officer J.P.
23rd March 1931 is celebrated as "Shaheed Diwas"'.
Srogank of Bhagat Singh
+ "Inquilab Zindabad" (Long Live Revolution).
(Note: Coined by Hasrat Mohani in 1921, popularized by Bhagat Singh).
Note: 30 Jan, the day Gandhiji died is also celebrated as "Shaheed Diwas".
Book written by Bhagat Singh: "Why Lam an Atheist"
In 2021, the Uttar Pradesh government renamed the "Kakori Train Robbery" as the "Kakori Train Action."

The word "Socialist" was added to the Hindustan Republican Association (HRA), which then became the Hindustan Socialist Republican Association (HSRA), reflecting the goal of establishing a socialist state.
Lala Lajpat Rai said: "Every blow aimed at me is a nail in the coffin of British imperialism."
Durgawati Devi (Durga Bhabhi) was a prominent member of the HSRA and actively participated in the revolutionary movement against British rule.
In 1930, Chittagong Armoury
Raid was led by Surya Sen (also known as Master Da).
Surya Sen was arrested in 1933 · Chandrashekhar Azad and hanged in Jan 1934. at Alfred Park
Women participants involved
It is now as Chdra- were: Pritilata Waddedar, shekhar Azad Park Kalpana Dutta, Suniti Choudhury, · where he shot himself Bina Das and Shanti Ghosh. on 27 February 1931 in Allahabad SIMON COMMISSION
Government of India Act 1919 was set to be reviewed by a Commission in 10 years but it announced the appointment of a Commission in just 8 years after the Act under the chairmanship of John Simon.
Note: Clement Attlee (Who later became PM of Britain) was the member of Simon Commission.
Recommendations of Simon Commission
+ Federal system of government should be introduced in India.
Separate Muslim electorate.
It rejected the separation of Sindh from Bombay.
+ The demand of frontier for equal status was also neglected.
It rejected 1/3rd Muslim seats in Central Assembly.
Madras Session of Congress of 1928
President: M. A. Ansari.
+ It was a special Session which passed a resolution, calling for boycott of Simon Commission.
Response to Simon Commission
The then Secretary, Birkenhead challenged the Indian leaders to draft their own Constitution.
Congress set up a committee under the chairmanship of Motilal Nehru which presented Nehru Report.
Demands in Nehru Report
1. Rejected Separate Electorate.
2. Demand for Dominion status.
3. Linguistic provinces, 19 Fundamental Rights, and a Responsible Government.
Delhi Proposals were given by Muslim League (1927).
Jinnah presented his 14 points (1929). Ignore Jinnah's points in the same manner she ignores you @).
SC Bose, J L Nehru and Srinivasa Iyengar formed Indian Independence League in 1928. The league was formed in opposition to the Nehru Report.
Those in support of Simon Commission: BR Ambedkar and Hindu Mahasabha (founded in 1915 by Madan Mohan Malaviya). Hindu Mahasabha initially supported the commission but later boycotted it.
Muddiman Committee (1924): Examined the working of Diarchy under the Government of India Act, 1919.
Linlithgow Commission (1926): Also known as the Royal Commission on Agriculture, focused on agricultural conditions in India.
Lee Commission (1924): Examined the recruitment and Indianization of Civil Services.
Bardoli Satyagraha (1928)
Leader: Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel.
Protest against a 22% hike in tax rates.
The title "Sardar" was given to him by the women of Bardoli.
Calcutta Session, 1928: In this Session, Nehru Report was accepted.
Irwin's Declaration, 1929; Thisis also known as "Deepavali Declaration". Viceroy Lord Irwin promised Dominion status in the future and a Round Table Conference post-Simon Commission's Report.
Delhi Manifesto, 1929; It outlined several key conditions by Indian leaders' for participating in the Round Table Conference.
Lahore Session, 1929: It was presided by J L Nehru.
Decisions taken:
1st Round Conference Table to be boycotted.

Goal: "Purna Swaraj" (Complete Independence). t+—— 31 Dec 1929: Flag was hoisted by J L Nehru on the banks of Ravi river with slogans of "Inquilab Zindabad". • —— 26 Jan 1930 was fixed as the First Independence Day.
Congress authorised to launch CDM.
—— Gandhi presented his 11 demands as an ultimatum before launching CDM. Irwin ignored them.
1. Arms Licenses: Issue licenses to Indians for self- protection.
2. Military Expenditure: Reduce military spending by 50%.
3. Political Prisoners: Release political prisoners.
4. Rupee-Pound Rate: Revise the exchange rate (Stronger Rupee).
5. Abolish Salt Law: Remove the tax and government monopoly on salt.
6. Civil Services: Reduce salaries of civil servants by 7. Coastal Shipping: Reserve coastal shipping for Indian merchants.
8. Import Duty: Impose custom duty on foreign cloth to protect Indian industry.
9. CID: Abolish or reform the Criminal Investigation Department (CID).
10. Land Revenue: Reduce land revenue.
11. Liquor: Total prohibition on intoxicants.
YOU NEED NOT MUG UP THESE 11 DEMANDS.
Dandi March was the beginning of Civil Disobedience Movement.
Time period: 12 March-6 April 1930.
Gandhi marched 241 miles along with 78 delegates from Sabarmati Ashram (Ahmedabad) to Dandi (Navsari) to violate Salt Law due to which it is also known as Salt Satyagraha.
The Dandi March received widespread international attention; Time Magazine initially mocked Mahatma Gandhi but later named him "Man of the Year" (1930).
Dharasana Satyagraha (1930)
Gandhi planned to raid the Dharasana but Gandhi got arrested on May 4, 1930 (before the raid).
After Gandhi's arrest, Abbas Tyabji led the raid in Darshana Salt Works. Following his arrest, it was led by Sarojini Naidu, Imam Sahib, and Manilal (Gandhi's son).
Role of Women:
Sarojini Naidu persuaded Gandhi to include women in the movement.
Kamaladevi Chattopadhyay famously told Gandhi: "Do not restrict this movement to men alone".
Salt was choosen as the theme because of the govt tax on salt and its monopoly over its production which revealed govt.'s oppressive face.
In Ryotwari Areas: Non-payment of revenue.
In Zamindari Areas: No chowkidar tax.
In Central Province: Violation of forest laws.
In Assam: Students protested against Cunningham Circular.
Cunningham Circular: A circular issued by J.R.
Cunningham forced students and parents to sign a pledge of "good behavior".
Participation of Leaders in Different States
Tamil Nadu: C Rajagopalachari (led Salt March from Trichinopoly to Vedaranniyam).
Orissa: Gopalbandhu Choudhary.
Bihar: Ambika Kant Sinha (Nakhas Pond was chosen as a site to violate Salt Law).
Peshawar: Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan or Badshah Khan or Frontier Gandhi He launched "Red Shirt Movement'.
Established: Khudai Khidmatgar (Servants of God).
Manipur & Nagaland: Rani Gaidinliu joined the anti-British struggle at the age of 13, led the Heraka Movement, and was imprisoned for 14 years (released after independence).
Prabhat Pheri, Vanar Sena, Manjari Sena were organised for mobilising the masses.
Gandhi-Irwin Pact 1931
This pact is also known as the Delhi Pact + It was signed on 5 March between Gandhi and Irwin.
Irwin's demands to Gandhi:
Participate in 2nd Round Table Conference.
Gandhi's demands (which were accepted by Irwin):
1. Release political prisoners, not convicted of violence.
2. Give the confiscated properties back to Indians which are not yet sold to third-parties.
3. Right to produce salt for personal consumption.
4. Right to make salt in coastal villages for personal consumption.
Gandhi's demands (which were not accepted by Irwin):
1. Public inquiry into police excesses.
2. Commutation of death sentence to Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev, and Rajguru.
It was held on 29 March 1931 - Presided by Sardar Patel.
'— Two resolutions were adopted: Fundamental Rights and National Economic Policy.
Round Table Conference (RTC)
RTCs were held in London to discuss about Simon Commission Report and future reforms for the country.
3 RTCs were held:
2nd: Sep 1931-Dec 1931 (it is the only RT where Gandhi and Congress participated).
B.R. Ambedkar attended all 3 RTCs.

2nd RTC failed due to non-acceptance of demands of Congress by British Government. Due to which Congress decided on 29th Dec 1931 to resume the CDM. The then Viceroy Willingdon also refused a meeting with Gandhi.
On 4th Jan 1932, Gandhi was arrested, finally on April 1934 Gandhi withdrew the CDM.
